titleText.es: Y yo podría sustituirte por fotos tuyas antiguas, de cuando parecías feliz.
titleText.en: And I could replace you with older pictures of you, from back when you looked happy.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive title text closely translates the official English title text. The raster also localizes the spoken exchange while leaving Photoshop as the established software name.

regions.labelEs: EN VEZ DE PEGARNOS EL ATRACÓN DE CONDUCIR HASTA AQUÍ, PODRÍAMOS HABER COGIDO NUESTRAS FOTOS DEL VERANO Y JUGAR CON EL AJUSTE DE "TINTE" DEL PHOTOSHOP.

applications.explanationEn: En vez de introduces pegarnos as the alternative action that could have been avoided.
Pegarnos identifies us as the people doing too much, while el atracón de conducir names the excessive activity.
Nos is attached to the unchanged dictionary form pegar and the result is written as one word.
Podríamos carries the tentative “we could” meaning, while haber stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
Haber is followed by the completed-action form cogido to place the taking before the unrealized possibility.
Nuestras uses the feminine plural form because fotos is feminine plural.

applications.exampleEs: JUGAR CON EL AJUSTE DE "TINTE" DEL PHOTOSHOP
applications.explanationEn: Jugar con presents the Photoshop hue setting as a control to experiment with rather than a game.
Calla is the affirmative informal singular command of callar.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; begins en vez de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: En belongs to the fixed three-word connector en vez de. Learn the connector as a unit rather than translating en as ordinary ‘in.’

example.es: Tomé té en vez de café.
example.en: I had tea instead of coffee.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that one option replaces another?
cards.answerEn: Put en vez de before the alternative that was not chosen: ‘instead of.’
cards.noteEn: A noun, pronoun, or unchanged action verb can follow: en vez de café, en vez de eso, en vez de llamar. The three words en vez de stay together.

example.es: Usamos el tren en vez del coche.
example.en: We used the train instead of the car.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; forms en vez de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: Vez often means an occurrence or time, but inside en vez de it helps form the fixed connector ‘instead of.’

example.es: Fuimos andando en vez de tomar el autobús.
example.en: We walked instead of taking the bus.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; completes en vez de, ‘instead of’
cards.noteEn: De finishes the connector en vez de and comes directly before the alternative that is not chosen.

example.es: Escribió un correo en vez de llamar.
example.en: She wrote an email instead of calling.

cards.answerEn: for us to indulge in; for us to go through (an excessive amount of something)
cards.noteEn: Pegarnos is pegar with nos attached. In pegarse un atracón, it does not mean physically hitting; the whole expression means indulging in or doing far too much of something.

example.es: Decidimos pegarnos un atracón de series.
example.en: We decided to binge on TV series.

cards.promptEs: pegarse un atracón de + cosa o actividad
cards.questionEn: How do you describe indulging in far too much of something at once?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching reflexive form of pegarse, then un atracón de and name the thing or activity.
cards.noteEn: The person marker changes: me pego, te pegas, se pega, nos pegamos. After de, an action stays in its unchanged dictionary form: un atracón de conducir. The expression is colloquial and often conveys excess or effort.

example.es: Nos pegamos un atracón de documentales.
example.en: We binged on documentaries.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

example.en: I want to help you.

cards.answerEn: the (masculine singular article)
binge; excessive amount done or consumed at once
cards.noteEn: Atracón can describe overeating, but it also extends to an excessive burst of another activity. It is masculine: un atracón.

example.es: Se dio un atracón de películas.
example.en: He went on a movie binge.

cards.answerEn: of; introduces the activity or thing involved in a binge
cards.noteEn: After atracón, de introduces what was consumed or done excessively. An action can follow in its unchanged dictionary form.

example.es: Nos dimos un atracón de ver películas.
example.en: We binged on watching movies.

cards.answerEn: to drive
cards.noteEn: Conducir is the unchanged dictionary form. It can name the activity of driving without identifying who performs it.

example.en: I prefer to drive during the day.

cards.answerEn: to; as far as (a destination)
cards.noteEn: Before a place, hasta marks the endpoint reached by movement. English often uses simply to, while as far as makes the endpoint emphasis explicit.

example.en: We walked to the station.

cards.answerEn: here
we could (a possibility or tentative suggestion)
cards.noteEn: Podríamos is the “would/could” form of poder for “we.” Poder keeps its whole dictionary form and adds -íamos. It often makes a suggestion sound tentative rather than stating a firm plan.

example.en: We could leave early.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

example.en: We can enter now.

cards.answerEn: have (unchanged helper form)
cards.noteEn: After a verb such as debería, haber remains in its dictionary form and combines with a completed-action form such as llamado or comido. In this construction, haber is a helper rather than the hay construction meaning “there is.”

example.en: He could have called.

cards.questionEn: How do you refer to an action that was already completed after another verb such as poder, deber, or parecer?
cards.answerEn: Use the unchanged helper haber followed by the completed-action form of the main verb.
cards.noteEn: The completed-action form is often called a participle: terminar becomes terminado, hacer becomes hecho, and ser becomes sido. After another verb, haber stays unchanged. The plus sign in the prompt means “followed by.”

example.en: It seems to have ended.

cards.answerEn: taken; picked up (completed-action form)
cards.noteEn: Cogido is the completed-action form of coger. With haber it forms a completed possibility such as podríamos haber cogido. In much of Latin America coger can sound sexual, but this source uses the ordinary Spain sense “take.”

example.en: We could have taken the train.

cards.answerEn: our (before feminine plural nouns)

cards.questionEn: How do you choose the Spanish form of ‘our’ before a noun?
cards.answerEn: Choose nuestro, nuestra, nuestros, or nuestras to match the gender and number of what is owned.
cards.noteEn: The form matches the owned noun, not the owners. Use nuestro before one masculine thing, nuestra before one feminine thing, nuestros before masculine or mixed plural things, and nuestras before feminine plural things.

example.en: Our suitcases are here.

cards.answerEn: photos
Photoshop is software used to alter images, and ‘Photoshopped’ commonly means digitally manipulated.
cards.noteEn: Edited images can contain clues such as inconsistent reflections, lighting, edges, or compression artifacts. The joke treats those familiar signs of manipulation as if they could prove that physical objects in the real world had been edited too.

cards.answerEn: from the (a time or period)
cards.noteEn: Del combines de and el. Here de marks a time or period as the source something comes from, rather than showing ownership.

example.en: We received a letter from the past.

cards.answerEn: summer
and
to play around; to experiment
cards.noteEn: With con and a tool, control, or idea, jugar can mean experimenting with it rather than playing a game.

example.es: Voy a jugar con los ajustes de color.
example.en: I am going to play around with the color settings.

cards.promptEs: jugar con + control, herramienta o idea
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone experiments or plays around with a control, tool, or idea?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of jugar followed by con and name what is being tried in different ways.
cards.noteEn: Jugar changes for the person and time, while con stays before the thing being adjusted or explored. In this use, jugar does not mean playing a game.

example.en: We are playing around with the design.

cards.answerEn: with; introduces what someone experiments with
cards.noteEn: In jugar con, con introduces the control, tool, or idea being tried in different ways.

example.en: Experiment with the lighting.

cards.answerEn: setting; adjustable control
cards.noteEn: In software or equipment, an ajuste is a setting that changes how something behaves or appears.

example.en: I changed the brightness setting.

cards.answerEn: no separate English word; links an item to its type
cards.noteEn: Spanish often uses de between an item and the noun that identifies its type. English often puts the type noun first instead: libro de historia becomes “history book.”

example.en: I bought a history book.

cards.answerEn: hue; color tint
cards.noteEn: Tinte can mean dye or tint. In an image-editing control, it refers to the hue or color cast applied to an image.

example.es: La foto tiene un tinte azul.
example.en: The photo has a blue tint.

cards.answerEn: of the
cards.noteEn: Spanish writes de followed by the masculine singular word el as the single word del.

example.es: El color del coche es rojo.
example.en: The color of the car is red.

cards.answerEn: Photoshop (image-editing software)
cards.noteEn: Photoshop is a product name retained in Spanish. Con Photoshop means that the software is the tool used for the edit.

example.en: She edited the photo with Photoshop.

cards.answerEn: hush; be quiet (informal singular command)
cards.noteEn: Calla tells one friend, relative, or other familiar person to stop talking. It comes from callar.

example.en: Be quiet for a moment, please.

cards.promptEs: orden afirmativa para tú: habla, come, escribe
cards.questionEn: How do you give one friend or familiar person a positive command?
cards.answerEn: Use the informal singular command form, often the same form used for “he” or “she” in the present.
cards.noteEn: For many regular verbs, -ar becomes -a and -er or -ir becomes -e: hablar becomes habla, comer becomes come, and escribir becomes escribe. Some common verbs are irregular or change their stem. Negative commands use a different form and are a separate pattern.

example.en: Open the window.

cards.answerEn: click
